blocks.content:
A Money Bill deals only with financial matters such as taxes and expenditure.
Important Points:
• Can be introduced only in Lok Sabha
• Requires prior recommendation of the President
• Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations
• Final authority lies with Lok Sabha
• Speaker certifies a Money Bill
A Money Bill deals only with financial matters such as taxes and expenditure.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Money Bills (Article 110) deal strictly with financial matters such as taxes and expenditure.
Money Bills require prior recommendation of the President and can only be introduced in Lok Sabha.
The Speaker of Lok Sabha holds the final authority and certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill.
Article 108 provides for a Joint Sitting to resolve deadlocks between the two Houses, presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha.
Joint Sittings are strictly not applicable to Money Bills and Constitutional Amendment Bills.
Parliamentary privileges grant MPs special rights such as freedom of speech in Parliament and immunity from court proceedings.

A joint sitting is called to resolve deadlock between the two Houses.
Important Points:
• Presided over by Speaker of Lok Sabha

items: Money Bills can ONLY be introduced in Lok Sabha and require the prior recommendation of the President.
Joint Sittings under Article 108 CANNOT be called for Money Bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills.
The Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over Joint Sittings and is the sole authority to certify a Money Bill.

blocks.content:
Parliamentary privileges are special rights and immunities enjoyed by members of Parliament.
Examples:
• Freedom of speech in Parliament
• Immunity from court proceedings
